chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tamimi narrated to me. He said: My father narrated to me. He said: My master Ali ibn Musa ibn Jafar narrated to me, from his father Musa ibn Jafar, from his father Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
It is not permissible for anyone to be in a state of janaba in this mosque except myself, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, and whoever is of my family, for they are from me.

key_terms.أهلي: My family (Ahli) - the Prophet's household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.المسجد: The Mosque - referring to the Prophet's Mosque (Masjid al-Nabawi) in Medina
key_terms.يجنب: Janaba - state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl (ritual bath) before prayer

ai.seo_question: Who was permitted to be in a state of janaba in the Prophet's Mosque?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declared that only he, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and their household members are permitted to be in a state of ritual impurity (janaba) in the Prophet's Mosque. This hadith, transmitted through the Golden Chain (silsilat al-dhahab) going through all the Imams from al-Ridha back to Imam Ali, establishes the unique spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt and their special relationship to the Prophet's Mosque in Medina.
word_analysis: be in a state of janaba
